newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan seen tendering for 108,000T soybeans, corn.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan seen tendering for 108,000T soybeans, corn.

text.p: Taiwan may tender for up to 92,000 tonnes of soybeans and 16,000 tonnes of corn this week, traders said on Monday.

A strong rise in Chicago soybean futures prices could prompt buyers to lock in supplies at current levels, they said. The July soybean contract on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) closed on Friday five U.S. cents up at US$8.89 a bushel.
"Buyers are considering whether to enter the market since soybean prices seem still on a uptrend," Steven Kuo, manager of Formosa Oilseed Processing Corp said.
Taiwan's Breakfast Soybeans Procurement Association Taichung division was considering tendering for 54,000 tonnes of U.S. or South America soybeans, traders said.
Taiwan's Hui Shung Group was negotiating with Continental Grain for a combined shipment of 38,000 tonnes of soybeanS and 16,000 tonnes of corn, traders said. The shipment is for late June delivery.

There were no other tenders scheduled as feed producers tried to trim their inventories due to weak demand following an outbreak of foot and mouth disease which has ravaged Taiwan's multi-billion dollary pork export industry.
Wheat buyers, on the other hand, were expected to stay on the sidelines this week.
U.S. Pacific Northwest freight rates were seen at about $11.50 per tonne while those from the Gulf of Mexico fetched a quote of about $21.00 a tonne, both for Panamax-sized March shipments.
